_what: A disposition for EVERY workflow in exports/instance-listing.json. Not a list of interesting flows - a TOTAL function over the instance, which is the only shape that cannot repeat the mistake this file exists to stop. Three times on 2026-08-23 a list built from something narrower than reality was trusted as reality: the exports directory, then the audit:* tag set, then 'everything with an ERP node' without asking which of those the programme was for.
_how_to_use: Add a row when a workflow appears; re-judge a row when its updatedAt moves. tools/manifest_vs_instance.py fails on a missing row, a stale row, and any disagreement with MANIFEST.json. It WARNS, and does not fail, on rows judged from name and description rather than from the workflow JSON - see erp_verified_from_export.

_dispositions.in-manifest: Audited by erp_compliance.py --all on every run, and required to be in MANIFEST.json (the tool checks both directions). Originally the six checks Moe named on 2026-08-23; the four flows remediated the same day under his 'stop at the 4 in flight' ruling joined them, because a flow brought up to the policy and then left out of the manifest is a flow whose compliance nothing re-checks - which is the drift this file exists to stop.
_dispositions.predecessor: A working check that one of the six reimplements. Out of scope by Moe 2026-08-23: the programme covers the rebuilds, not the flows they replace.
_dispositions.other-audit-programme: Tagged audit work Moe excluded from the six.
_dispositions.infrastructure: The lease, the ask-code channel and its executor, the breaker sandbox. Not audits.
_dispositions.scratch: Throwaway probes, diagnostics and smoke tests.
_dispositions.out-of-programme-erp-audit: An audit check that DOES reach ERP and is not among the six. Reported as a standing warning, because it is the honest answer to "what else could hit ERP" and the load policy has never been applied to it.
_dispositions.out-of-programme-no-erp: Reporting/alerting/accounting workflow with no evident ERP surface.
_dispositions.skill-built-outside-programme: Produced by the erp-audit-flow-builder skill but NOT remediated. The sharpest category here: the skill built them, so the policy is the standard they were meant to meet. Reported as a named warning with a count. As of 2026-08-23 one flow is left in it, and it is here because it has no ERP surface at all, not because it was excused.
_dispositions.delete-me: A throwaway probe or diagnostic that reaches ERP and should not exist any more. Exempt from MANIFEST.json because the fix is deletion, not compliance - but named by the guard on every run so "we will clean those up" does not quietly become never.

_erp_verified_from_export: true only where the workflow JSON is held in exports/ and was read. Everywhere else the ERP judgement is from the name and description, which is weaker and is counted rather than hidden.

_skill_built: THE TRACKER. Which flows the erp-audit-flow-builder skill produced, which nothing recorded until 2026-08-23 - and not recording it is how five skill-built flows sat outside the compliance programme without anyone noticing. The discriminator is meta.aiBuilderAssisted true with meta.builderVariant 'mcp' in the workflow's own payload, NOT the name, the tag or the creation date: 'CC Overstay Fines - generated v1' and 'Applicant Real Ticket Refund Audit' are both audit checks with similar names and only the first is skill-built. 'unverified' means nobody has opened the payload; it is counted, never assumed either way.
_the_rule: A flow that the skill built AND that reaches ERP MUST be in MANIFEST.json, so erp_compliance.py --all audits it forever. tools/manifest_vs_instance.py FAILS when it is not. That is the whole tracker: not a list someone maintains out of diligence, but a rule that breaks the build.
_sweep: Provenance and ERP contact re-established from the workflow payloads on 2026-08-23 by a full sweep (exports/provenance-sweep.json), not from names. It corrected this file in two directions: it found the estate's worst ERP offender wrongly recorded as not skill-built, and four rows claiming ERP contact that make no ERP call at all. 32 of 103 workflows could not be read at all - see _unreachable.
_unreachable: 32 workflows refuse get_workflow_details with 'Workflow is not available in MCP' (availableInMCP unset). They are recorded skill_built 'unreachable' rather than guessed. Seven are ACTIVE. This is a third of the estate that no checker in this repo can see, and it is the largest remaining blind spot - larger than anything the policy currently covers. Enable MCP access on a workflow's card to bring it into view.
_manifest_exempt: Why a skill-built ERP-touching flow is legitimately absent from MANIFEST.json. The guard accepts a recorded reason and refuses SILENCE, which is the state every flow missed on 2026-08-23 was in. An exemption is a decision someone made and signed; an absent row is nobody having looked.
_scope_ruling_2026_08_23: Moe, asked with the numbers in front of him whether 'all skill-generated flows comply' should reach the 8 newly-found ones: STOP AT THE FOUR IN FLIGHT. Travel Assist and the seven SDR flows carry manifest_exempt reasons rather than being quietly left out, so the guard is green because a decision was made and not because nobody looked. Exempt is not compliant. Every one of those eight still reaches ERP unpaced and unleased, and two of them are live.
